## T3. Residual ON − OFF: significance

| Depth | Δ (pp) | SE | Welch t | df | p (Welch) | p (exact permutation) | 95% CI (pp) | Cohen d |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | -1.38 | 0.85 | -1.62 | 3.8 | 0.185 | 0.200 | [-3.81, +1.04] | -1.32 |
| 20 | +3.26 | 0.57 | +5.72 | 2.0 | 0.029 | 0.100 | [+0.81, +5.70] | +4.67 |

A 95% CI that contains 0 means the direction of the effect is not established at that n.

Interaction (effect at depth 20 minus effect at depth 8): +4.64 pp, SE 1.03, Welch-Satterthwaite t=+4.53, df=5.7, p=0.004, 95% CI [+2.10, +7.18]. This is the test that backs a "residual value depends on depth" claim.

## T5. Train-loss difference (ON − OFF) at the final epoch

| Depth | Mean Δ train loss | Welch t | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | +0.024 | +1.73 | 0.214 |
| 20 | -0.079 | -10.42 | 0.002 |

Negative Δ means the residual arm reaches lower training loss (the degradation-problem prediction: a training, not only a test, effect).

## T7. Comparison table (assignment reporting convention)

| Model | Optimizer | Augmentation | Epochs | Params | Val acc (mean±SD) | Test acc (mean±SD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ToggleResNet depth 8, residual ON | Adam (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4) | RandomCrop+Flip | 10 | 75,290 | 73.73 ± 1.17 | 73.73 ± 1.17 |
| ToggleResNet depth 8, residual OFF | Adam (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4) | RandomCrop+Flip | 10 | 75,290 | 75.12 ± 0.90 | 75.12 ± 0.90 |
| ToggleResNet depth 20, residual ON | Adam (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4) | RandomCrop+Flip | 10 | 269,722 | 81.29 ± 0.03 | 81.29 ± 0.03 |
| ToggleResNet depth 20, residual OFF | Adam (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4) | RandomCrop+Flip | 10 | 269,722 | 78.03 ± 0.99 | 78.03 ± 0.99 |

Val acc equals test acc here because the pipeline evaluates one held-out set (the CIFAR-10 test set) for both checkpoint selection and reporting; this selection effect must be disclosed in the report.
